nodes.label: RED-GREEN-REFACTOR Cycle
nodes.rationale: The cycle enforces that a test is compiled and executed (not just written) before implementation starts (RED gate), and that tests pass before refactoring begins (GREEN gate), ensuring tests verify real behavior not imagined behavior.

nodes.label: Tracer Bullet TDD Pattern
nodes.rationale: Write one test that confirms one thing, proving the end-to-end path works before expanding coverage. Prevents horizontal slicing anti-pattern.

nodes.label: Horizontal Slicing Anti-Pattern
nodes.rationale: Writing all tests first then all implementation produces tests that verify imagined behavior, test data structure shapes rather than outcomes, and break on refactors that don't change anything the user sees.

nodes.label: Git Checkpoint Commits at TDD Stages
nodes.rationale: One commit per confirmed RED, one per confirmed GREEN, and one after refactoring. Provides a clear audit trail of the TDD cycle and prevents squashing until the full cycle is complete.
nodes.norm_label: git checkpoint commits at tdd stages

nodes.label: Mock at System Boundaries Only
nodes.rationale: Mocking only external APIs, databases, time/randomness, and file system (at boundaries) while never mocking your own classes/modules or internal collaborators keeps tests reliable and decoupled from implementation.

nodes.label: SDK-Style Interfaces for Mockability
nodes.rationale: Specific functions per external operation (SDK-style) rather than a generic fetcher allow each mock to return one specific shape, require no conditional logic in test setup, and provide type safety per endpoint.

nodes.label: Deep Module Design Principle
nodes.rationale: From 'A Philosophy of Software Design': deep module = small interface + lots of implementation. Reduces the number of methods exposed, simplifies parameters, and hides complexity inside. Contrasts with shallow module (large interface, thin implementation) which should be avoided.

nodes.label: Behavior-Based Testing (Test Through Public Interfaces)
nodes.rationale: Tests should exercise real code paths through public APIs, describing WHAT the system does not HOW. Integration-style tests using real interfaces survive internal refactors because they don't care about internal structure.

nodes.label: Dependency Injection for Testability
nodes.rationale: Accept dependencies rather than create them internally, and return results rather than produce side effects. Fewer methods and fewer params means simpler test setup.

nodes.label: Accept Interfaces Return Structs Go Idiom
nodes.rationale: Functions accept interface parameters (flexibility, testability) and return concrete types (avoids hiding implementation details unnecessarily). Interfaces are defined where they are used (consumer package), not in the provider.
nodes.norm_label: accept interfaces return structs go idiom

nodes.label: Clean Architecture Layers (domain → usecase → infra)
nodes.rationale: Strict layer separation with domain at the center, usecase depending on domain, infra depending on usecase interfaces. Prevents wrong-direction imports and keeps business logic independent of infrastructure concerns.

nodes.label: Functional Options Pattern
nodes.rationale: Functional options provide extensible constructors with defaults without breaking existing callers when new options are added.

nodes.label: Error Wrapping with Context
nodes.rationale: Use fmt.Errorf with %w to wrap errors with context, enabling errors.Is and errors.As for precise error type checking while preserving the error chain.

nodes.label: Context Propagation and Cancellation
nodes.rationale: Context is always the first parameter (never stored in structs), used for cancellation, deadlines, and timeouts to prevent goroutine leaks.

nodes.label: Table-Driven Tests Pattern
nodes.rationale: Standard Go test pattern using a slice of test case structs with t.Run subtests. Enables comprehensive coverage with minimal code and readable test names.

nodes.label: Fuzz Testing with testing.F
nodes.rationale: Go 1.18+ fuzz testing with seed corpus and property-based assertions finds edge cases that enumerated table tests miss.

nodes.label: Interface-Based Mocking in Go
nodes.rationale: Mock using struct with func fields implementing the interface, without third-party libraries, keeping mocks close to the test and type-safe.

nodes.label: Python Clean Architecture (domain → usecase → infra → entrypoints)
nodes.rationale: Four-layer clean architecture for Python: domain, usecase, infra, entrypoints. Protocol-based abstractions in usecase layer enable testability without concrete dependencies.
nodes.norm_label: python clean architecture (domain → usecase → infra → entrypoints)

nodes.label: Protocol-Based Duck Typing
nodes.rationale: Python Protocols (structural subtyping) allow defining interfaces without inheritance, enabling duck-typed dependency injection that satisfies mypy strict type checking.

nodes.label: EAFP (Easier to Ask Forgiveness Than Permission)
nodes.rationale: Python idiom: try the operation and handle the exception rather than pre-checking conditions (LBYL). More Pythonic and avoids race conditions.
nodes.norm_label: eafp (easier to ask forgiveness than permission)

nodes.label: pytest Fixture Design
nodes.rationale: Fixtures with scope (function/module/session) and setup/teardown via yield eliminate test duplication. Shared fixtures live in conftest.py, scoped to the test level they serve.

nodes.label: Parametrize for Table-Driven Python Tests
nodes.rationale: @pytest.mark.parametrize is the Python equivalent of Go table-driven tests, providing multiple input/output combinations in a single test function with readable IDs.

nodes.label: Integration Test Isolation with Markers
nodes.rationale: @pytest.mark.integration separates slow/external-dependency tests from fast unit tests. Integration tests are excluded from default pytest runs and can be run explicitly.

nodes.label: Decision Tree Interview Process
nodes.rationale: Walks a plan through scope, domain model, API contract, business logic, data layer, CLI surface, observability, auth, deployment, dependencies, error handling, and tests branches before implementation. Resolves architecture before data layer, data layer before API contract.

nodes.label: ADR Writing Criteria (Hard to Reverse + Surprising + Real Trade-off)
nodes.rationale: Only write an ADR when all three are true: hard to reverse, surprising without context, and a real trade-off was made. Avoids documentation noise for obvious or easy-to-reverse decisions.
nodes.norm_label: adr writing criteria (hard to reverse + surprising + real trade-off)

nodes.label: PRD Template Structure
nodes.rationale: PRD includes Problem Statement, Solution, User Stories, Implementation Decisions, Testing Decisions, Out of Scope, and Further Notes. Does not include file paths or code snippets (they go stale fast) except for prototype snippets encoding decisions more precisely than prose.

nodes.label: Deep Module Extraction During PRD
nodes.rationale: PRD authoring includes actively identifying opportunities to extract deep modules that can be tested in isolation — linking architecture planning to testability requirements.

nodes.label: HITL vs AFK Issue Classification
nodes.rationale: HITL (Human-in-the-Loop) slices require human interaction (architectural decision, design review). AFK slices can be implemented and merged without human interaction. Prefer AFK over HITL to maximize autonomous agent execution.

nodes.label: MCP vs REST API Fallback Pattern for Jira
nodes.rationale: Prefer mcp-atlassian MCP server (exposes tools directly) over direct REST curl calls. REST fallback exists for environments where MCP is not configured.
nodes.norm_label: mcp vs rest api fallback pattern for jira

nodes.label: Guardrails Three Modes (Careful / Freeze / Guard)
nodes.rationale: Three escalating protection levels: Careful (intercepts destructive commands), Freeze (locks file edits to directory), Guard (both combined). Uses PreToolUse hooks on Bash, Write, Edit, and MultiEdit tool calls.

nodes.label: Parallel Agent Dispatch Pattern
nodes.rationale: Agents run simultaneously (parallel Agent tool calls, not TeamCreate), each independently receiving agent file content plus task description. Max 5 agents per team to avoid diminishing returns and excessive token usage.

nodes.label: Mandatory Prometheus Metrics Requirement
nodes.rationale: Every gRPC method and REST endpoint must emit Prometheus metrics. No API or RPC ships without metrics. Go uses grpc.UnaryInterceptor; Python instruments at the entrypoint layer, never inside usecase or domain.

nodes.label: gRPC + grpc-gateway Service Structure
nodes.rationale: All REST is generated via grpc-gateway (hand-rolled HTTP handlers are forbidden). buf generate regenerates stubs from proto; generated files under gen/ must never be manually edited.

nodes.label: Ralph Loop Iterative Development Workflow
nodes.rationale: Implementation does not start until the PRD exists in docs/prd/. Ralph loop prompts reference the PRD path as the source of truth for completion criteria.

nodes.label: Scope Discipline Rules
nodes.rationale: Fix the reported bug only, do not add abstraction layers or new packages not required by current task, do not introduce feature flags or backwards-compatibility shims for hypothetical future use. Prevents scope creep.

nodes.label: Ralph Loop Workflow
nodes.rationale: Used for well-defined iterative tasks with programmatically verifiable success criteria (tests passing, lint clean). Not for debugging incidents, tasks requiring mid-way design decisions, or one-shot queries.
